5: 1. "Yield Test" sheet: weigh the whole product as purchased, clean it, weigh what's left and weigh separately the byproducts you will actually use.
6: 2. The workbook gives you the yield, the trim loss, the AP/EP factor and the NET cost per clean pound, with and without using the byproducts.
7: 3. Compare that net cost with the price on the invoice: the difference is what the pound that goes to the pass really costs you.
8: 4. "Cooking Loss Test" sheet: weigh the piece raw and again cooked and rested; you get the cost per pound of the finished product.
9: 5. "My Trim Loss Table" sheet: type your measured trim loss and the "Trim loss you use" column switches on its own from the reference to yours.
10: 6. Carry the trim loss from the "Trim loss you use" column to the "Trim loss (%)" column of recipe-cost-card.xlsx: that's where it turns into money.
11: Where the reference trim loss figures come from
12: A working reference table for professional use (compiled from professional kitchen trim loss tables and from the trim loss article on aichef.pro/blog). It isn't an official table: measure your own with the yield test.
14: Weights are in pounds (lb) and prices per pound; amounts carry no currency symbol and are in your currency. Every price in this workbook is pre-tax, as in the rest of the pack. In the US, sales tax you pay on supplies is a cost: include it in the price. If you're registered for VAT or GST/HST (UK, Canada, Australia), leave the reclaimable tax out: it's cash flow, not cost.
